answer: Verifiers can run surprise load tests: they hand every identity a burst of real paid jobs at the same instant and log each one's throughput. Independent agents run on their own hardware, so their speeds stay uncorrelated. A sybil orchard grown on one shared GPU cluster slows down together, like shale layers cracking along the same seam. When the delta between identities' latency curves stays near zero across tests, they are merged into one reward share, so extra clones earn nothing.
